bank.q: A visitor asks what makes the town unusual. Which answer introduces the point most naturally?

d: I will now describe the parade in June.

bank.q: You are explaining why you chose shared living. Which sounds most natural?

bank.a: Somewhere in the region of four thousand attended.
d: Exactly four thousand attended, more or less.

I cannot, I am busy then.

bank.q: You are describing a plan that is agreed but not yet booked. Which is most accurate?
bank.a: We are planning to move in the spring, though nothing is fixed.
d: We are moving in the spring.
We will move in the spring.

bank.q: Someone predicts an outcome you doubt. Which reply questions it without flat contradiction?
bank.a: I am not so sure — what makes you think that?
d: I do not agree with you.

bank.q: You want to say time matters more to you than money. Which expresses it best?
bank.a: I would rather have the afternoon back than the overtime.
d: I do not like money very much.

d: You need to decide right now.

bank.q: You are writing a balanced opinion essay. Which sentence opens the counter-argument best?
bank.a: There is, however, a serious objection to this.
d: But that argument is completely wrong.
I will now say the other side.
Some people think differently, of course.

bank.q: You want to state a view without claiming certainty. Which is most appropriate in writing?
bank.a: The evidence suggests, though it does not prove, that costs would fall.
d: I feel costs are going to fall.

bank.q: Which closing sentence best suits a balanced essay?
bank.a: On balance the benefits appear to outweigh the risks, provided the funding holds.
d: So that is my opinion about it.
In conclusion, I am definitely right.
To sum up, both sides have points.

bank.a: It was an absolutely freezing morning.
d: It was a very freezing morning.

bank.q: You are describing what the polar night does to daily life. Which sentence is most B2?
bank.a: You stop trusting the clock and start organising the day around whatever light there is.
d: It is very dark so life is difficult.
The day is dark and you must do things.
There is no sun and people feel bad.

bank.q: You want to say a change happened slowly but was very large. Which fits?
bank.a: It happened gradually, but the difference by March was considerable.
d: It was slight but happened dramatically.
Gradually it was a slight big change.

bank.q: A visitor says the winter must be depressing. Which reply politely complicates that?
bank.a: People assume that, but a lot of us actually prefer it to the endless summer light.
d: No, you are wrong about that.
Yes, it is very depressing here.
That is what everybody says wrongly.

bank.q: You are describing your sleep pattern to a doctor. Which is most useful to them?
bank.a: I fall asleep easily but wake at about four and cannot get back to sleep.
d: I sleep badly most of the time.

bank.q: A friend says they never sleep. Which reply invites detail rather than closing it down?
bank.a: Is it getting to sleep that is the problem, or staying asleep?
d: You should go to bed earlier.

bank.q: You want to contrast a past habit with what you do now. Which sentence does it best?
bank.a: I used to work late into the night; these days I am in bed by ten.
d: I worked late, now I go to bed early.
I would work late and I go to bed.
Before late, now ten o'clock in bed.
